posts.content: Track opponents’ actions. As a good player, cooperate with likely-good players; defect when the chance they are selfish is high enough that protecting good-player payoff outweighs cooperation gains.

I will cooperate with everyone, including selfish players: cooperation among good players yields the highest shared total, while mutual cooperation also provides a useful basis for identifying exploitative behavior.
As selfish, maximize my payoff by defecting every round.
As a good player, prioritize joint welfare: cooperate with unknown opponents, update beliefs from observed actions, and defect against opponents strongly indicated to be selfish.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good players and defect against likely selfish players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players, since mutual defection gives me 1 rather than 0 when facing a selfish defector.

As a good player, prioritize welfare of good players: cooperate with likely good players, defect against likely selfish defectors. Update beliefs from observed actions, but remember each pairing is one-off.

Good-good: C maximizes combined welfare. Against selfish D, choose D for payoff 1 rather than 0; selfish D is dominant, so observed D is strong evidence of selfishness. Cooperate with unknowns; update from their actions.
Favor cooperation with likely good players; adapt to observed actions, while avoiding being repeatedly exploited by defectors.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players; against likely-selfish players, defect to protect good-player payoff. Update from observed actions.

I am good; unknown opponents should generally receive C because mutual cooperation yields strong welfare. Use observed action history to infer selfishness, and choose D against likely selfish opponents when it improves total good-player payoff.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating a C as evidence of a good opponent.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize shared welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents, who should defect to maximize their own payoff.
For good-player welfare, cooperate with opponents more likely good than selfish; defect when evidence makes selfishness more likely.

I am good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones, since selfish opponents should defect and mutual defection gives me 1 instead of 0. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for uncertainty and one-shot pairings.

Cooperate with P3 if their selfishness probability is below 0.5; against a selfish defector, D limits our good-player loss. C from P2 and P6 is strong evidence they’re good, so account for the reduced selfishness probability among remaining players.
I’ll cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff, and defect against opponents likely to be selfish or exploitative.
Defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
P3’s defection raises suspicion; P5’s cooperation supports good. Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize shared good-player welfare, defect against likely selfish ones.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update from observed actions.
P2 is unobserved; cooperate, then update from their action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Since selfish players favor D, update beliefs from observed actions and keep cooperation when evidence is absent.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown opponents; mutual cooperation creates the greatest welfare when both are good. Defect only when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish, to avoid giving them an advantage.

As a good player, cooperate with good opponents to maximize their welfare; defect against selfish opponents, who optimally defect. Any selfish player’s observed cooperation would be unexpected, so treat observed C as strong evidence they are good.
P2 and P6 played C, so treat them as good. P3’s D is suspicious but not conclusive; update cautiously. Cooperate with likely-good players, and defect when it better protects good-player welfare.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; selfish players have an incentive to defect, so defect against likely-selfish opponents. Use observed actions to update beliefs.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize shared welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed behavior and use cooperation when the opponent is more likely good.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. A selfish player should defect, so observed cooperation is strong evidence they are good.
P10 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence makes selfishness more likely than not.

I am good: cooperate with likely-good opponents to preserve mutual welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents, since their D makes C yield 0 while D yields 1. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Prioritize total welfare of good players: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, while allowing for strategic uncertainty.
Cooperate with P1 if likely good; defect if evidence makes selfishness more likely. Prior mutual cooperation with P7, P8, and P10 strongly indicates they are good.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. Their one-shot payoff-maximizing action is D; observed C is strong evidence they are good.
Treat P3’s D as strong evidence they are selfish. For unknown opponents, cooperate unless evidence raises selfishness probability above the welfare threshold; use observed actions to update.
Continue cooperating with likely-good players; defect against opponents likely selfish to protect the good players’ total payoff.
As a selfish player, I will defect to maximize my payoff.
Against a likely good opponent, cooperate to preserve mutual welfare; against a likely selfish opponent, defect. Update beliefs from observed play, accounting for the welfare of all good players.
For good opponents, cooperation maximizes their combined payoff; against likely-selfish opponents, defect to protect good players. Use observed actions as evidence and update beliefs.
P4 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness. The four opponents who cooperated with me are likely good. Update beliefs from actions and prioritize welfare among good players.
All four opponents observed choosing C are good. Cooperate with P10 absent evidence they are selfish; defect only when evidence supports selfishness.

Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish ones. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions, since a single defection is evidence but not proof.
All four encountered players cooperated, strongly indicating they are good. P5 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
As a good player, cooperate with P7 absent evidence they are selfish; cooperation maximizes combined welfare with a good opponent, while defection is preferable against a selfish defector.

For P4, cooperate unless evidence puts selfishness above roughly 0.5; good-good cooperation raises shared welfare, while D limits loss against a selfish defector. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; against likely selfish defectors, defect to avoid earning zero. Update from observed actions, but a single defection is not conclusive.
Defect this round; D maximizes my payoff regardless of P7’s action.
P1 has no observed history, so I’ll cooperate under the prior and continue prioritizing shared welfare with likely good players.
For good opponents, mutual cooperation maximizes their combined payoff. Against likely-selfish opponents, defect to protect good-player payoffs; update beliefs from observed actions.
P9 is untested. Cooperate with known cooperators; against an untested opponent, weigh the chance they are good against likely selfish defection, and prioritize total payoff of actual good players.
P3 is unobserved. Choose the action that maximizes expected good-player welfare, accounting for the chance they are selfish; update from their action afterward.
Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good opponents and defect against likely selfish ones. Treat P3’s defection as evidence of selfishness; P2 is unobserved.

Five encountered players cooperated against my C, strongly identifying them as good. P6 remains unobserved; cooperate unless evidence raises their selfishness probability above the welfare-relevant threshold.

Assuming selfish players defect in one-shot encounters, the five opponents observed cooperating are good. P5 has no action evidence; cooperate unless new evidence makes selfishness more likely than goodness.

As good, cooperate with a good opponent and defect against a selfish defector; choose C when estimated selfishness is below 0.5. Treat observed C as strong evidence of good, and D as strong but not infallible evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect if the opponent is more likely selfish, using observed behavior to update beliefs.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.

Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize shared good-player welfare; defect when an opponent is likely selfish, especially if they are expected to defect. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
Against good players, cooperate to maximize their joint payoff; defect against known selfish players. P2 is unobserved, so cooperate absent evidence otherwise.
P3 is untested. Cooperate with them if choosing now: mutual cooperation has the best joint payoff if they are good, while their action will reveal useful evidence.
P3’s D is evidence of selfishness; cooperate with P8 absent direct evidence, and use observed action to update beliefs.
Prioritize total welfare of good players: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect when the opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. Update cautiously from observed behavior.
Six known cooperators are good. P2, P3, and P4 share the remaining selfishness probability; defect against P4 if selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P5 also cooperated, so all six observed cooperators are good. With only P1, P3, and P8 unobserved, cooperate with P1 absent contrary evidence; defect only against a likely selfish defector.
Against P7, cooperate unless evidence makes defection better for good-player welfare. Treat observed actions as evidence, not proof of role.
P3’s defection against my C is evidence of selfishness; P1, P5, P6, P7, P10 cooperated when met. For P4, weigh prior uncertainty; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness.
Defect against P9; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P2 is unobserved; cooperate under the prior, and keep prioritizing total welfare of good players.
P6 is unobserved and likely good; cooperate absent strong contrary evidence. P3’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but don’t overgeneralize; revise beliefs using the prior and observed play.
P5 is untested. Cooperate: this supports greater welfare if they are good, and update beliefs from their action.
For P1, cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; defection is worthwhile only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P3’s D is strong evidence about P3, not P1.
Prioritize total payoff of good players: cooperate if P10 seems good; defect if evidence makes selfishness likely. With no prior encounter evidence, use the prior cautiously.
Seven opponents chose C, so they are good. Exactly one of P2 and P3 is selfish; each has probability 0.5. Against P3, C and D tie in expected good-player welfare; choose C.

P1’s defection is evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P8 is unobserved; cooperate absent contrary evidence, since mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
For P5, use observed record if available; choose C if likely good, D if selfishness probability exceeds 0.5. Good-good C raises combined good welfare; against selfish D, D limits our loss.
Cooperate with P9 unless evidence suggests they are selfish; use observed play to guide future choices.
Continue defecting; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P10’s action.
P7 is unobserved. Choose the action that best protects total good-player welfare: cooperate if P7 is more likely good, defect if more likely selfish.
P1 is unobserved, so absent strong evidence favor cooperation: mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update from observed actions; defect if there is strong reason to expect P1 is selfish.
P3 is the strongest selfish candidate; P8 is untested. Cooperate with P8 absent strong evidence otherwise, and update from their action.
P1 and P3’s defections are evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P4 is unobserved; avoid assuming every defector is selfish. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support shared welfare.
Prioritize welfare of good players. P2 and P3’s defections suggest selfishness, but don’t infer too much from one encounter. Against P6, cooperate absent clear evidence they are selfish.
P3 is unobserved. Cooperate if their selfishness chance is below 0.5; defect above it. Selfish players strictly defect, while mutual cooperation maximizes welfare when both are good.
P9 previously cooperated, so treat them as good and choose C in the final round.
P6 reciprocated C earlier; cooperate in the final round to preserve mutual benefit for good players.
Final encounter: defect; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P4’s action.
P3 defected in our only prior encounter. In this final round, defect against P3: it protects good-player welfare if P3 defects and gains against a selfish opponent.
P7 cooperated when we met, strong evidence they are good. I’ll cooperate to maximize good players’ joint payoff.
P2 cooperated when we met earlier, so treat them as likely good and favor C to maximize shared welfare.
P5 chose C in round 3, so they are good. Cooperate with P5 to maximize shared good-player welfare.
Final round: cooperate with P10. Their prior cooperation is consistent with being good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare, and defection is only preferable if they are selfish.
Final round: prioritize good-player welfare. P1 previously cooperated, so cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P8 previously cooperated, so under selfish players’ payoff-maximizing behavior they are good. Cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs; update beliefs from observed actions and defect only when protecting good-player welfare favors it.
Cooperate with likely good players; adapt to observed behavior to maximize good players’ total payoff.
As a selfish player, defect to maximize my payoff in each simultaneous encounter.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player payoffs; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed play and adapt to likely selfish behavior.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent when that best supports likely shared welfare; update from observed play and defect when evidence strongly suggests selfishness.
Cooperate absent evidence: this maximizes expected total payoff when the opponent is more likely good; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown opponents: mutual cooperation best serves good players, and the prior makes P10 more likely good than selfish. Defect if evidence indicates a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, remembering each pairing is one-off.
Cooperate with unknown opponents while their selfishness probability is below the welfare tradeoff; update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate to maximize good players’ joint payoff; adapt to observed behavior and defect only when an opponent is likely selfish.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when shared welfare is more likely; defect when evidence indicates a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total payoff among good players; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with an unknown opponent: cooperation raises total welfare if they are good, while the prior makes that more likely than selfishness. Defect only when evidence strongly suggests a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. P9’s cooperation indicates they are good; update remaining beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate with unknown players while the chance they are good exceeds the welfare tradeoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when the expected payoff to good players is higher; defect if the opponent is sufficiently likely selfish.
Defect each round: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents. P3’s defection raises suspicion, while P5’s cooperation lowers it.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve their combined payoff; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support shared welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with P5 absent evidence of selfishness; use encounter actions to update beliefs and defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P8: the prior and two observed cooperations make P8 more likely good than selfish. Mutual cooperation benefits good players most; defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. P2 and P9 cooperated, so treat them as good and update the remaining probabilities.
Cooperate with unknowns when the chance they’re good makes cooperation better for good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when it is expected to raise total payoff among good players; update beliefs from observed play and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize shared welfare; defect only when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. P3’s defection raises suspicion; P5 and P10’s cooperation lowers it.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ joint payoff; observed cooperation strongly identifies good players. Continue updating beliefs from play.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: shared welfare favors C when they are likely good. Treat observed cooperators as good and update beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate with P2 absent evidence of selfishness; the observed C actions identify P5, P6, and P9 as good.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; use observed actions to update identity beliefs, while accounting for uncertainty.
Cooperate with P1: the three observed cooperators are good, while P1’s selfishness probability remains below the threshold where defection yields greater expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate: the remaining probability that P6 is good makes mutual cooperation more valuable for good-player welfare than defecting; defect only when evidence makes selfishness likely.
Cooperate with P8: their estimated selfishness is below the welfare tradeoff. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and update cautiously from defections.
Cooperate to support the total payoff of good players; update beliefs from observed actions and defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. P6 has no observed history, so cooperate under the prior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent while selfishness is less likely than not; observed cooperators are likely good. Update beliefs from play and prioritize total welfare of good players.
Cooperate with the unobserved P10: the evidence makes selfishness less likely than goodness, and cooperation best supports total payoff among good players.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.

Cooperate with P5: given the observed cooperations and the conditioned prior, P5 is more likely good than selfish. Mutual cooperation benefits good players; defect only if evidence makes selfishness more likely.

Cooperate with P7 absent evidence they are selfish; observed cooperation from P2, P4, P6, and P9 identifies them as good. Continue updating from actions, accounting for the prior over selfish-player counts.
Cooperate with P4: their estimated selfishness is below the welfare tradeoff. Update beliefs from observed actions and favor cooperation with likely-good players.
Defect when the opponent is more likely selfish than good; otherwise cooperate to maximize the good players’ combined payoff.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action by P7.

Cooperate with P1 under the current belief: mutual cooperation benefits good players more than unilateral defection. Update identity beliefs from observed play and defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P9: most likely they are good, and C supports greater total welfare with a good opponent. Update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with P3: given the evidence, mutual cooperation with a good opponent outweighs the small gain from defecting against a selfish one.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

Cooperate with P6: they are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. The five observed cooperators are inferred good; unobserved players share the remaining selfishness probability.

Cooperate with P5: after five opponents cooperated, P5’s selfishness probability is 0.46875, so cooperation has a slight expected welfare advantage. Selfish players defect; observed cooperation identifies good players.
Defect against P10 because the remaining-role evidence makes selfishness likely; cooperate with known likely-good players and update beliefs from actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their combined payoff; adapt to observed actions and defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.

Cooperate with P9, who has no observed history and is more likely good; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Prior observed cooperation rules out selfishness under optimal play, while P3’s defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and only a very high selfishness probability favors defection. Use observed actions to update beliefs.
Cooperate with P3: after conditioning on the six observed cooperators being good, P3 is more likely good than selfish, and C maximizes expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P8 absent direct evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Treat P3’s D as evidence and update beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes selfishness more likely. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P4: their selfishness probability is below the welfare-relevant 0.5 threshold. The six observed cooperators are good; the remaining possible selfishness is shared among P2, P3, and P4.
Cooperate with confirmed good players; defect against an opponent with substantial chance of being selfish, since they will defect and defection protects good-player payoff.

Defect when the estimated chance the opponent is selfish exceeds the welfare tradeoff; otherwise cooperate. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defections as strong, but imperfect, evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P2 has no observed history. Prior cooperation by six opponents rules them out as selfish; P3’s defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate with P6 absent strong evidence of selfishness; cooperation benefits good players when both are good. Treat P3’s defection as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness.

The observed defection makes P3 likely selfish; prior counts then place substantial selfishness probability on the two untested players. Defect against P5 because the expected good-player welfare favors D at this belief level.
Cooperate with P1: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective, and current evidence does not make P1 sufficiently likely selfish.
Cooperate with P10 absent evidence of selfishness; observed defections by P2 and P3 raise their selfishness estimates, while cooperation is suggestive but not conclusive evidence of being good.
Only P2 and P3 can be selfish, with equal probability. Against P3, C and D tie in expected welfare for good players; choose C.

Cooperate with P8 absent evidence they are selfish; six observed cooperators are good under the selfish players’ payoff-maximizing behavior. Update beliefs from actions while allowing good players to defect strategically.
Cooperate with P5 while their estimated selfishness is below the welfare tradeoff; use observed actions to update beliefs.
Cooperate with P9: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation best supports the good players’ total payoff.
Defect; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P10’s action.
Cooperate with P7: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare, and P7 is more likely good. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; P3’s defection makes P3 more suspect.
The observed defections strongly identify P3 and P6 as selfish. Given the allowed selfish counts and the known-good cooperators, this implies P1 is selfish too; defect to protect good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with P8 absent strong evidence of selfishness; their action history is unknown, while prior cooperation from others is evidence they are likely good. Update beliefs from the encounter.
Cooperate with P4 absent direct evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Keep P1 and P3’s defections as evidence about them, not others.

Prioritize total payoff of good players: cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P2 and P3’s defections raise my estimates, while P6 has no direct evidence.
Cooperate with P2: the observed defection makes P3 more likely selfish, leaving P2 below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare.

The seven observed cooperators are good if selfish players always defect. The sole selfish player is therefore P1 or P3; P1’s defection makes them more likely. Cooperate with P3 to maximize good-player welfare.

Cooperate with P9, whose observed cooperation strongly indicates they are good. In this final round, favor C when the opponent is more likely good; report D players as uncertain rather than treating defection as proof of role.
Cooperate with P6, whose earlier cooperation suggests they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ combined payoff.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect against P3: their prior defection identifies them as selfish under payoff-maximizing play, and D protects my payoff whether they cooperate or defect.
Cooperate with P7, whose observed cooperation identifies them as good. The two observed defectors share the remaining selfishness probability; cooperate when the opponent is likely good.
P2 previously cooperated, so I infer they are good and choose C to maximize shared welfare.
Cooperate with P5: their observed C is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation supports the shared welfare objective.
Cooperate with P10: their earlier cooperation is evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P1: they previously cooperated, and mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare.
P8’s prior cooperation strongly indicates they are good. Cooperate to maximize good-player welfare; the remaining selfishness uncertainty is between P1 and P3.

Cooperated with likely-good players; defected when evidence suggested the opponent was selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection as suggestive but not conclusive.
Cooperated with players who cooperated; treated P3’s defection as evidence of selfishness and defected once to avoid exploitation.
Defected every round to maximize my payoff, earning 46. Most opponents cooperated; P4 defected in our final encounter.
Cooperated with opponents who cooperated; defected against P3 after their prior defection, prioritizing welfare of good players.

Cooperated with observed cooperators; defected once against an opponent judged likely selfish. Defections by P3 and P6 remain indistinguishable evidence, so split the remaining selfishness belief equally.
Cooperated to support shared welfare, updating beliefs from observed actions; defected once when the expected welfare of good players favored it.
Cooperated to support shared welfare; treated observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare; treated P2 and P3’s defections as evidence of selfishness, while keeping uncertainty between them.
Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare; P3’s defection was the only observed selfish action.

Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defected only when an opponent seemed likely selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as strong evidence of being good.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players; defected when evidence suggested the opponent was selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection as suggestive but not conclusive.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with players who cooperated; treated P3’s defection as evidence of selfishness and defected once to avoid exploitation.

P3.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my payoff, earning 46. Most opponents cooperated; P4 defected in our final encounter.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with opponents who cooperated; defected against P3 after their prior defection, prioritizing welfare of good players.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators; defected once against an opponent judged likely selfish. Defections by P3 and P6 remain indistinguishable evidence, so split the remaining selfishness belief equally.

P6.strategy: Cooperated to support shared welfare, updating beliefs from observed actions; defected once when the expected welfare of good players favored it.

P7.strategy: Cooperated to support shared welfare; treated observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.

P8.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare; treated P2 and P3’s defections as evidence of selfishness, while keeping uncertainty between them.

P9.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare; P3’s defection was the only observed selfish action.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defected only when an opponent seemed likely selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as strong evidence of being good.
